---
title: "Differential expression: one comparison"
description: >
  Read a DE table from edgeR, DESeq2, limma or Seurat; volcano and MA plots;
  up- and down-regulated gene lists and ranked lists for GSEA.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")
```

**Question:** which genes change between two conditions, by how much, and how
does that depend on their expression level?

| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| `standardize_de()` | read any DE table into standard columns (used by every DE plot) |
| `plot_volcano()` | fold change against significance |
| `plot_ma()` | fold change against mean expression |
| `filter_de_genes()` | up- and down-regulated genes as two tables |
| `rank_de_genes()`, `generate_de_rank_file()` | genes ranked by signed significance, for GSEA |

**Data:** macrophages of 6 donors, naive or stimulated with interferon-γ
(IFN-γ) ([Alasoo et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-018-0046-7)).
The same comparison is tested with edgeR and with DESeq2, paired by donor
(design `~ donor + condition`), to show that the plots read either.

```{r data}
mac <- docs_macrophage()
keep <- mac$samples$condition %in% c("naive", "IFNg")
counts <- filter_low_expression_genes(mac$counts[, keep], min_group_size = 6)
samples <- droplevels(mac$samples[keep, ])

# edgeR quasi-likelihood test
design <- model.matrix(~ donor + condition, data = samples)
y <- edgeR::normLibSizes(edgeR::DGEList(counts))
fit <- edgeR::glmQLFit(y, design)
test <- edgeR::glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "conditionIFNg")
de_edger <- edgeR::topTags(test, n = Inf)

# DESeq2 Wald test, with shrunken fold changes
dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    counts,
    samples,
    design = ~ donor + condition
)
dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE)
de_deseq <- DESeq2::results(dds, name = "condition_IFNg_vs_naive")
shrunk <- DESeq2::lfcShrink(
    dds,
    coef = "condition_IFNg_vs_naive",
    type = "normal",
    quiet = TRUE
)
de_deseq$log2FoldChange_shrunk <- shrunk$log2FoldChange
```

Fold-change shrinkage pulls the noisy fold changes of lowly expressed genes
towards 0. `type = "normal"` is built into DESeq2; its authors recommend
`type = "apeglm"` (package apeglm) or `"ashr"` when installed.

## Reading DE tables

Every DE plot of the package reads its input with `standardize_de()`, which
recognises edgeR, DESeq2, limma and Seurat tables from their column names and
returns standard columns (`feature`, `logfc`, `pvalue`, `padj`, `mean_expr`,
then the table's other columns):

```{r standardize, message = TRUE}
head(standardize_de(de_edger), 3)
head(standardize_de(de_deseq, logfc.col = "log2FoldChange_shrunk"), 3)
```

| method | log fold change | p-value | adjusted p | mean expression |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| edgeR | `logFC` | `PValue` | `FDR` | `logCPM` (log2) |
| DESeq2 | `log2FoldChange` | `pvalue` | `padj` | `baseMean` (linear) |
| limma | `logFC` | `P.Value` | `adj.P.Val` | `AveExpr` (log2) |
| Seurat | `avg_log2FC` | `p_val` | `p_val_adj` | none |

Any other table works with the columns given explicitly (`logfc.col`,
`p.col`, `padj.col`, `mean.col`, `feature.col`); the same arguments are
accepted by every DE plot. p-values of exactly 0 (underflow) are replaced by
a tenth of the smallest non-zero value, and NA p-values (DESeq2's
independent filtering) are treated as not significant.

## Volcano plot

```{r volcano}
plot_volcano(de_edger, label.n = 6)
```

The y-axis is the −log10 **adjusted** p-value, the value that decides
significance, so the dashed line is the `padj.cutoff`. The `label.n` most
significant genes of each direction are labelled (10 by default), among them
interferon-γ targets such as *IRF1*, *APOL4* and *UBD*.

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `logfc.cutoff`

A minimum absolute fold change for significance, drawn as dashed lines:

```{r volcano-cutoff}
plot_volcano(de_edger, logfc.cutoff = 2, label.n = 5)
```

#### `label`

`label = "selected"` labels only the genes given, significant or not;
`label = "top"` with `label.features` adds them to the top genes:

```{r volcano-selected}
plot_volcano(
    de_edger,
    label = "selected",
    label.features = c("STAT1", "IRF1", "CIITA", "HLA-DRA", "ACTB")
)
```

#### `label.rank`

The top genes ranked by `"padj"` (default), `"logfc"` or `"product"` of both:

```{r volcano-rank}
plot_volcano(de_edger, label.rank = "product", label.n = 6)
```

#### `annotate.counts`

`"arrow"` names the directions with arrows and counts at the top (and drops
the legend); `"none"` hides the counts:

```{r volcano-arrow}
plot_volcano(
    de_edger,
    annotate.counts = "arrow",
    up.label = "Up in IFN-γ",
    down.label = "Down in IFN-γ",
    label.n = 5
)
```

#### `cols`

Colours named `up`, `down`, `ns` (any of them):

```{r volcano-cols}
plot_volcano(
    de_deseq,
    logfc.col = "log2FoldChange_shrunk",
    label = "none",
    cols = c(up = "#B5338A", down = "#2C5DA8")
)
```

## MA plot

Fold change against mean expression shows how both depend on the expression
level. edgeR's `logCPM` is already log2 and drawn as it is:

```{r ma}
plot_ma(de_edger, label.n = 5)
```

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### DESeq2, shrunken

DESeq2's `baseMean` is linear and drawn on a log10 axis (`mean.scale` is
taken from the method). With shrunken fold changes, the lowly expressed genes
on the left no longer fan out:

```{r ma-shrunk}
plot_ma(
    de_deseq,
    logfc.col = "log2FoldChange_shrunk",
    label.n = 5
)
```

#### DESeq2, unshrunken

The same genes without shrinkage, for comparison:

```{r ma-raw}
plot_ma(de_deseq, label = "none")
```

#### `trend`

A robust trend line (lowess) through all genes: a trend away from 0 would
point to an expression-dependent bias, such as a normalization problem.

```{r ma-trend}
plot_ma(de_edger, trend = TRUE, label = "none")
```

## Gene lists

`filter_de_genes()` splits a DE table into up- and down-regulated genes (the
rows of the table, with all its columns), by adjusted p-value and absolute
fold change:

```{r filter, message = TRUE}
de_lists <- filter_de_genes(
    as.data.frame(de_edger),
    padj.cutoff = 0.05,
    logfc.cutoff = 1
)
vapply(de_lists, nrow, integer(1))
head(rownames(de_lists$up_reg))
```

`rank_de_genes()` ranks all genes by the signed significance
−log10(adjusted p) × sign(log fold change), the "pi-value": strongly
up-regulated genes first, strongly down-regulated last.
`generate_de_rank_file()` returns (and with `file`, writes) the two-column
`.rnk` table of the GSEA desktop application:

```{r rank}
ranked <- rank_de_genes(as.data.frame(de_edger))
head(ranked[c("logFC", "FDR", "piValue", "rank")], 3)
# file = "ifng.rnk" writes it
rnk <- generate_de_rank_file(as.data.frame(de_edger))
head(rnk, 3)
```

For fgsea or clusterProfiler, the ranking is a named vector:
`setNames(rnk$rank, rnk$GeneName)` (see [Gene-set enrichment](enrichment.html)).
Many genes share the largest −log10 adjusted p-values; ranking by the test
statistic (edgeR `F` with the fold change sign, DESeq2 `stat`) breaks such
ties and is a common alternative.

These three functions take the same `method`, `logfc.col` and `padj.col` as
the plots (renamed in 0.10.0 from `de_method`, `log2fc_col`, `pvalue_col`;
the old names still work, with a deprecation warning).
